value adds to its electioneering.ELECTROMAGNETIC COMPATIBILITY (EMC) – Part 4-6: Testing and measurement techniques – Immunity to conducted disturbances, induced by radio-frequency fields

1 Scope

This part of IEC 61000 relates to the conducted immunity requirements of electrical and electronic equipment to electromagnetic disturbances coming from intended radio-frequency (RF) transmitters in the frequency range 150 kHz up to 80 MHz.

NOTE 1 Product committees might decide to use the methods described in this document also for frequencies up to 230 MHz (see Annex B) although the methods and test instrumentation are intended to be used in the frequency range up to 80 MHz.

Equipment not having at least one conducting wire or cable (such as mains supply, signal line or earth connection) which can couple the equipment to the disturbing RF fields is excluded from the scope of this document.

NOTE 2 Test methods are specified in this part of IEC 61000 to assess the effect that conducted disturbing signals, induced by electromagnetic radiation, have on the equipment concerned. The simulation and measurement of these conducted disturbances are not adequately exact for the quantitative determination of effects. The test methods specified are structured for the primary objective of establishing adequate repeatability of results at various facilities for quantitative analysis of effects.

The object of this document is to establish a common reference for evaluating the functional immunity of electrical and electronic equipment when subjected to conducted disturbances induced by RF fields. The test method in this document describes a consistent method to assess the immunity of an equipment or system against a specified phenomenon.

NOTE 3 As described in IEC Guide 107, this document is a basic EMC publication for use by product committees of the IEC. As also stated in Guide 107, the IEC product committees are responsible for determining whether this immunity test standard should be applied or not, and if applied, they are responsible for determining the appropriate test levels and performance criteria.

2 Normative references

The following documents are referred to in the text in such a way that some or all of their content constitutes requirements of this document. For dated references, only the edition cited applies. For undated references, the latest edition of the referenced document (including any amendments) applies.

CISPR 16-1-2, *Specification for radio disturbance and immunity measuring apparatus and methods – Part 1-2: Radio disturbance and immunity measuring apparatus – Coupling devices for conducted disturbance measurements*

3 Terms and definitions

For the purposes of this document, the following terms and definitions apply.

ISO and IEC maintain terminology databases for use in standardization at the following addresses:
- IEC Electropedia: available at https://www.electropedia.org/
- ISO Online Browsing platform: available at https://www.iso.org/obp

**Table 4 – Usage of CDNs**

| Line type             | Examples                                                                 | CDN type                          |
|---------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| Power supply (AC and DC) | AC mains, DC in industrial installations, earth connection             | CDN-Mx (see Figure D.2)             |
| Screened cables     | Coaxial cables, cables used for LAN and USB connections, cablers for audio systems | CDN-Sx (see Figure D.1             |
| Unscreened balanced lines | ISDN lines, telephone lines                                                      | CDN-Tx (see Figure D.4, Figure D.5, Figure D.7 and Annex H) |
| Unscreened unbalanced lines | Any line not belonging to other groups                                                    | CDN-AFx or CDN-Mx (see Figure D.3 and Figure D.6) |

6.2.2.2 CDNs for power supply lines

CDNs are recommended for all power supply connections. However, for high-power (current ≥ 16 A) or complex supply systems (multi-phase or various parallel supply voltages), other injection methods may be selected.

The disturbing signal shall be coupled to the supply lines, using type CDN-M1 (single wire), CDN-M2 (two wires) or CDN-M3 (three wires), or equivalent networks (see Annex D). Similar networks can be specified for a three-phase mains system. The coupling circuit is shown in Figure 7.

NOTE The performance of the CDN can be degraded by saturation of the magnetic material due to current drawn by the EUT, especially when using CDN-M1. This can be avoided if the magnetizing effect of the forward current is cancelled by that due to the return current.

WARNING — The capacitors used within the CDNs bridge live parts. As a result, high leakage currents can occur and safety connections from the CDN to the reference ground plane are mandatory (in some cases, these connections might be provided by the construction of the CDN).

6.2.2.3 CDNs for unscreened balanced lines

For coupling and decoupling disturbing signals to an unscreened cable with balanced lines, a CDN-T2, CDN-T4 or CDN-T8 shall be used as a CDN. Figure D.4, Figure D.5 and Figure D.7 show these possibilities:

- CDN-T2 for a cable with one symmetrical pair (two wires);
- CDN-T4 for a cable with two symmetrical pairs (four wires);
- CDN-T8 for a cable with four symmetrical pairs (eight wires).

The number of symmetrical pairs is determined by the cable connected to the port.

Other CDN-Tx networks may be used if they are suitable for the intended frequency range and satisfy the requirements of 6.2.1. For example, the differential-to-common-mode conversion loss of the CDNs should have a larger value than the specified conversion ratio of the cable to be installed or equipment connected to the installed cable. If different conversion ratios are specified for cable and equipment, then the smaller value applies. Often, the clamp injection needs to be applied to multi-pair balanced cables if suitable CDNs are not available.

**7.3 EUT comprising several units**

Equipment comprising several units, which are interconnected, shall be tested using one of the following methods.

- Preferred method: Each sub-unit shall be treated and tested separately as an EUT (see 7.2), considering all others as AE. Coupling and decoupling devices (or CDNs) shall be placed on the cables (according to 7.4.1) of the sub-units considered as the EUT. All sub-units shall be tested in turn.
- Alternative method: Sub-units that are always connected together by short cables, i.e. ≤ 0.4 m, and that are part of the equipment to be tested, can be considered as one EUT. No conducted immunity test shall be performed on their interconnecting cables, these cables being regarded as internal cables of the system. See Figure 19.

**Figure 20 - Rules for selecting the injection method**

Testing shall be performed with the EUT, including selected cables for testing, installed, arranged and operated in a manner consistent with typical applications. CDNs not listed in this document, but meeting the requirements of this document, may also be used.

Where several cables coming from the EUT are in close proximity over a length of more than 10 m or are routed from the EUT to other equipment in a cable tray or conduit, they should be treated as one cable, regardless of cable types present. If the bundle of cables is too large for testing as one cable, they should be separated by cable type or function (e.g. signal, mains, screened, etc.) and at least one cable of each type or function tested individually.

If a product committee decides that a certain kind of coupling and decoupling device is more appropriate for cables connected to a particular family of products, then that choice (justified on a technical basis) takes precedence. These devices shall be described in the product standard. Examples of CDNs are described in Annex D.

#### 7.4.3 Ports to be tested

In any one test, only two 150 Ω networks are required, one for signal injection, one for signal return path. It is not necessary to connect unterminated CDNs to all other EUT ports which are not yet undergoing RF test signal injection or return path. These other ports can instead be left open (unless the technical function of the EUT requires a treatment of these ports for operation) until they shall be used for injection of the test signal. At that time the suitable CDN can be connected and used for injection on each of such ports in turn. The CDN used for injection of the test signal can be moved between different ports as they are tested. When a CDN is removed from a port, it may be replaced by a decoupling network.

If the EUT has multiple identical ports (same input or output electronic circuits, loads, connected equipment, etc.), at least one of these ports shall be selected for testing to ensure that all different types of ports are covered.

### 7.5 CDN injection application

When using the CDN injection, the following measures shall be taken.

a) If the AE is directly connected to the EUT (e.g. no decoupling on the connection between them as shown in Figure 21a)) then it is to be placed on an insulating support 0,1 m ± 0,05 m above the reference ground plane and grounded via a terminated CDN.

If the EUT has multiple AEs directly connected to it, only one AE shall be terminated in this manner. Other directly connected AEs shall have all other connections decoupled. This ensures that there is only one loop terminated with 150 Ω at each end.

b) If the AE is connected to the EUT via a CDN, then its arrangement is not generally critical and it can be connected to the reference ground plane in accordance with the AE's and EUT's installation requirements.

c) One CDN shall be connected to the port intended to be tested and one CDN with 50 Ω termination shall be connected to another port. Decoupling networks shall be installed on all other ports to which cables are attached. In this manner there is only one loop terminated with 150 Ω at each end.

d) The CDN to be terminated shall be chosen according to the following priority:

1. i)CDN-M1 used for connection of the earth terminal;
2. ii)CDN-M3, CDN-M4, or CDN-M5 used for mains (class I equipment);
3. iii)CDN-Sn (\(n = 1,2,3...\)): if the EUT has several CDN-S\(n\) ports, the port which is closest to the port selected for injection (shortest geometrical distance) shall be used;
4. iv)CDN-M2 used for AC or DC mains (class II equipment);
5. v)Other CDN connected to the port which is the closest to the port selected for injection (shortest geometrical distance).

NOTE 1 - Annex I gives guidance for an alternative CDN injection process for specific products.

e) If the EUT has only one port, that port is connected to the CDN used for injection.

NOTE 2 - The capacitive coupling path from the EUT to the reference ground plane provides the return path for the test signal.

The maximum instantaneous pressure in the CEt installation shall not exceed 35 kPa and shall not be exceeded within 5 minutes. The High Pressure Limit Valve (HPLV) in the bilevel piping upstream of the separation section is provided with an alarm interlock to prevent the HPLV from sealing off until the level of the preparation-to-utilization (P-T) mixture at the regulator is reduced to within 20 mm. The output from the HPLV is connected to a thermal flow meter, and signals from the flowmeter are fed back 8 seconds after signals from the CEt analogue output from torque measurement are fed back into the CEt. If this response time is slower than 2 minutes, the CEt OER for the next dosing step shall not be operated until the HPLV is opened 5 minutes following the signals from the flowmeter. 7.7	Direct injection application

When using direct injection to screened cables, the following measures shall be taken.

- The EUT shall be placed on an insulating support of 0,1 m height above the reference ground plane.
- On the cable being tested, a decoupling clamp as specified in Clause A.3 shall be placed between the injection point and the AE, as close as possible to the injection point. A second port of the EUT shall be loaded with 150 Ω (see 7.5 and Figure 6 for details). On all other cables attached to the EUT decoupling networks shall be installed. When left open, a CDN is considered a decoupling network. See also 6.2.5.
- The injection point shall be located between 0,1 m and 0,3 m from the geometric projection of the EUT onto the reference ground plane.
- The test signal shall be injected directly onto the shield of the cable through a 100 Ω resistor (see 6.2.4).

8	Test procedure

The EUT shall be tested within its intended operating and climatic conditions.

The radiation from the test setup can be subject to local interference regulations. If the radiated energy exceeds the permitted level, the test shall be performed in a shielded enclosure.

**10 Text report**

The text report shall contain all the information necessary to reproduce the text. In particular, the following shall be recorded:

- identification of the EUT and any associated equipment, for example brand name, product type, serial number, software, etc.;
- the size of the EUT;
- representative operating conditions of the EUT;
- whether the EUT is tested as a single or multiple unit;
- the types of interconnecting cables, including their length, and the interface port of the EUT to which they were connected;
- any specific conditions for use, for example cable length or type, shielding or grounding, or EUT operating conditions, which are required to achieve compliance;
- the recovery time of the EUT if necessary;
- the type of test facility used and the position of the EUT, AE(s) and coupling and decoupling devices;
- identification of the test equipment, for example brand name, product type, serial number, software, etc.;
- the coupling and decoupling devices used on each cable;
- for each injection port, indicate which decoupling devices were terminated in 50 Ω;
- a description of the EUT exercising method;
- any specific conditions necessary to enable the test to be performed;
- the frequency range of application of the test;
- the rate of sweep frequency, dwell time and frequency steps;
- the test level set;
- the number of tones and grouping used (if applicable);
- the performance level specified by the accompanying documents;
- the performance criteria that have been applied;
- any effects on the EUT observed during or after application of the test disturbance and the duration for which these effects persist;
- the rationale for the pass/fail decision.

}^ angled relationship, and the hypothesis fits best. This is a proxy for the true relationship, with the slope and intercept calculated from the line fitting model compared to the actual data points.

The model is significant, and the results support the hypothesis. It appears that the fitted model with a positive slope and intercept of 1.9 and 0.098, respectively, and a slope of 1.9 looks the best. The corresponding x-value is 1.52, which is not a significant value given the other parameters. Therefore, the null hypothesis can be rejected, and the population mean would need to be approximately 0.048535984 meters to meet the average and standard deviation mentioned in the hypothesis test.

In summary, there is strong evidence that a linear relationship exists between the variables collected from the IEE continuous curve interval gripping clamp analysis. As the sample size was relatively small, it is difficult to draw definitive conclusions, but the modeling work supports the hypothesis, with two potential explanations: either the IEE continuous curve interval gripping clamp is not ideal for this particular application, or the IEE continuous curve interval gripping clamp performs better in other applications normally handled by the biaxial grip clamp. To further validate this result and the applicability of the IEE continuous curve interval gripping clamp, data from a complete IEE clamp assembly will need to be collected for testing.

A.2.2.1 Impedance

A.2.2.1.1 Measurement setup

The test jig as specified in A.2.1 shall be used for the impedance measurement. The clamp (i.e., injection port) shall be terminated with a 50 Ω load and placed into the test jig, see Figure A.6. For impedance measurement the EM clamp is treated as a two-port device which can be characterized by its S-parameters \(S_{11}\), \(S_{12}\), \(S_{21}\), and \(S_{22}\) measured in a 50 Ω system using a network analyzer. Prior to the measurement the network analyzer shall be normalized at the cable ends (to be connected to the jig) using a standard through-open-short-matched (TOSM) method with an appropriate calibration kit. The length between the cable end and the clamp reference point shall be respected by a port offset of the vector network analyzer (VNA) or by other means.

The following is a list of examples:

\begin{itemize}
  \item For a cable only connected to a keyboard (extended dimension ≥ λ/10) powered from a battery-operated personal computer, with a coiled cable having a length of 4 m, the start frequency should be 6,67 MHz. The keyboard should be covered by the artificial hand. For a mouse having just 2 m of cable, the start frequency would be 15 MHz, etc.
  \item A pocket calculator with an AC/DC adapter option, should be tested on the mains side of the adapter from 150 kHz upwards. The pocket calculator should be covered by the artificial hand.
  \item A hand-held battery-supplied multimeter which can have connections to ground should be tested on its cables from 150 kHz upwards. The multimeter should be covered by the artificial hand.
  \item A double insulated (mains) compact disc player which can be connected to an audio receiver, connected to insulated loudspeaker boxes, but also having an antenna input terminal which can be connected to ground should be tested on both mains supply and audio cable(s) from 150 kHz upwards.
  \item A burglar alarm having various insulated sensors distributed through a building, of which the maximum length of cable may extend 200 m (EUT's specification) should be tested on these cables from 150 kHz upwards.
\end{itemize}

finding.The text on the given page discusses the final step in the validation of certain components, specifically the test level used. It explains that the test level is the level designed to exert the limitations on the testing of equipment. The final test level is proposed as Level 4, which is specified in relation to the test result of Class 1 electronic magnetic radiation environment. This final test level can be evaluated by the manufacturer using either a suitable level of test result or a reference test; the determination made on the basis of these two methods is deemed acceptable.

The final step in the validation is to obtain a thorough understanding of the effect of the proposed test level for the equipment in that class on the handling of potentially hazardous environments. However, even if there is no operating license for these environments, it is understood that the operators will be responsible for this task. Detailed and complete documentation supporting this task is expected to be submitted to the relevant authorities or authorities in designated timeframes based on the class of the equipment.

The document also covers the conditions related to test level evaluation for equipment provided for research and other definitive uses, specifically for tests to be carried out at the laboratory establishment level. For new equipment, the test level should be tested on the basis of a theoretical study and evaluation using equipment following specified test conditions.

In case the test level is modified, the manufacturer bears responsibility for the necessary action to inform the affected parties accordingly. This adjustment is to take place using the survey equipment provided to test operators. The severity of the relevant equipment can be determined based on the alteration of test parameters and other factors. The choice of the level to be applied should be reasoned by the manufacturer and the specifications for individual items.

The document ends with a meticulously detailed schedule of tests based on Commission Directive 2014/35/EU, which involves configuration change testing and calculations using the IEC 60068 load and interface resistance fluctuations.

The 12th Edition of the IEC 61000 series covers not only phototypes, but also parameters related to products used in automotive environments. The document includes several test results that provide a broad understanding of the order of magnitude of failures in certain devices, mainly beverages.

The document also outlines the responsibilities of why the authors share or have shared each batch of parts. It deals with the influence of temperature on devices and some test results that can be considered errors when the equipment is used in a narrow pressure range. This information is intended to guide the use of protective devices in connection with equipment, particularly for small equipment where protective relays should not be used as self-relays. The test levels are not limits at the point of use and are devices that allow performance of a typical, acceptable test situation. However, users must ensure that the test results are used only as a confidence, and less than a reliable determination should be made.

One of the primary objectives of the GOST standard (GOST 18231-92) is to ensure the accuracy of measurements and test results. The English text provides a thorough explanation of the final step in the validation process and details the final steps of the process, ensuring that equipment is tested at the proper test level and that operators and users are aware of the risks and consequences of insufficient testing.

#### C.3.3 Input quantities and calculation examples for expanded uncertainty

The examples below assume that the same instrumentation used in the test level-setting procedure is used for generating the voltage test level (the measurement setup for the test level-setting is that depicted in Figure 16 and Figure G.5), except for the measuring instrument, which is absent during the test. However, the uncertainty contributions that would exist, if different instrumentation is used, are shown in Table G.1 to Table G.8 but their values can be set to zero (see notes below Table G.1 to Table G.8).

Therefore, it has to be recognized that the contributions which apply for the level-setting process and for the test will possibly not be the same. This leads to (slightly) different uncertainty budgets for each process.

Table G.1 to Table G.8 give examples of an uncertainty budget for voltage level-setting. Each uncertainty budget consists of two parts, the uncertainty for level-setting and the uncertainty for test. The level-setting process determines the relation between \( U_x \) and \( U_{mr} \) (see Figure G.1.) During the test process, \( U_x \) is reproduced.

**G.4 Expression of the calculated measurement uncertainty and its application**

MU is calculated in logarithmic units to make it homogeneous with the uncertainty contributions to the test level uncertainty (e.g. voltmeter amplitude specification and adapter insertion loss calibration) usually expressed in dB. Hence, the best estimate also shall be expressed in logarithmic units (e.g. dB(μV)).

The voltage test level shall be reported in terms of the best estimate of the voltage and its expanded uncertainty. The best estimate shall be the average of the voltage $U_0$ over the relevant frequency range.

The following is an example of the presentation of measurement uncertainty:

In logarithmic units:

\[U_0 = 129,5 \, \text{dB(μV)} \pm 1,36 \, \text{dB (example for CDN injection)}\]

This corresponds in linear scale to:

\[U_0 = 3 \, V + (17 \, %) - (14,5 \, %) \]

.## Annex H
(informative)

## Testing with multiple signals

### H.1 General

Annex H provides information related to testing EUTs with multiple signals during one dwell cycle in order to reduce the overall test time. It provides information related to:

* the intermodulation effects created by multiple signals,
* the power required to generate multiple signals,
* the level-setting requirements,
* linearity checks, and
* EUT performance criteria with multiple signals.

### H.2 Intermodulation

Intermodulation can be generated in a system with nonlinearities. The intermodulation between each frequency component will form additional signals at frequencies that are not just at harmonic frequencies (integer multiples) of each frequency, but also at the sum and difference frequencies of the original frequencies and at multiples of those sum and difference frequencies.

The result of this intermodulation is the creation of unwanted signals in the form of sidebands (centered around fundamental and harmonic frequencies).

These unwanted signals shall not significantly affect the quality of the susceptibility test.

This can be seen in the graph in Figure H.1 and mathematically represented as follows:

\[\begin{array}{c}
1 \\
2 \\
f_1 \\
2f_1 - f_2
\end{array}
\quad \text{and at} \quad \begin{array}{c}
3 \\
3 \\
-2f_1 \\
-2f_2
\end{array}\]

\[\begin{array}{c}
2 \\
3 \\
2f_1 + f_2 \\
2f_2 - f_1
\end{array}\]

}}}{</script> typically involves the use of a database system that includes various modules for data storage, retrieval, manipulation, and analysis. These modules can include relational databases, data warehouses, data lakes, and NoSQL databases. The database system also supports indexing mechanisms to enable fast retrieval of data based on specific search criteria. Additionally, query languages are often used to interact with the database system, such as SQL (Structured Query Language) for relational databases and HiveQL (Hive Query Language) for data warehouses. It's also common for the database system to incorporate built-in data transformation and data packaging tools to manage data formats and structure. This makes it easier to move and transform data between different systems and tools within the enterprise. In more complex scenarios, database systems may also support distributed databases, multi-model databases, and cloud-based databases. Database systems can offer scalability, high availability, and fraud detection capabilities through mechanisms like replication, queuing, and automated maintenance. This leads to better performance and reliability in the event of hardware failures or network disruptions. Overall, database systems provide a reliable and scalable storage and retrieval mechanism for managing large volumes of data in various sectors, including finance, transportation, healthcare, and more.

To withstand a blow of this magnitude, the furnace door must withstand an average impact speed of 918 m/s20. The maximum temperature that the steel door can withstand is 1080 degC due to the melting temperature of martensitic stainless steel, which happens at around 1150 degC (around 2200 degF).Calculating the heat flux through the furnace door:

\[ W = \frac{Q}{A} \]where:
\( W \) is the heat flux (W/m²)
\( Q \) is the heat supplied (J/s)
\( A \) is the face area of the furnace door (m²)

\[ A = \pi r^2 \]

\[ r = \sqrt{\frac{Q}{W}} \]Substitute the given values:, \( Q = 90 \, \text{kJ} \)):,,\[ X = \pi \times 0.4 \times r^2 \times 1080 / 918 \, \text{m/s} \]\[ \therefore r = \sqrt{\frac{90}{5180}} \approx 0.06 \, \text{m} \]Finally, substitute \( L \) (latent heat, the heat required to change the state of the object without changing its temperature):,,\[ r \approx 0.056 \, \text{m} \]Finally, calculate the heat flux,,\[ W = \frac{90}{5180} \times \pi \times 0.056^2 \times 1080 \approx 4.5 \, \text{kJ/s} \]Using these results, it is typical for a 500 mm thick furnace door made from martensitic stainless steel to withstand an average impact velocity of around 50 m/s.

It's also worth noting that the output heat flux within the furnace door is limited by the strength of the thermal barrier within the furnace, and so is substantially less than the input heat flux given above (the furnace door is not a black body as it's not necessarily possible to raise the temperature inside the furnace to such a high level). For a 500 mm thick furnace door, the power input to the furnace (and hence the heat flux) through the floor is usually less than 100 kW of electricity and this would translate into a power supply of a few tens of kilowatts.

— 76 —From the selected values given in the analysis above, if the furnace door is to withstand a temperature rise of 100 degC within one minute of input, it's necessary for the efficiency of the system, and hence for the input wattage, to be above a few megawatts. Since this level of wattage would almost certainly demand a steel furnace that is in itself a research reactor (a furnace design that would be optimised for maintaining the temperature of its interior with a cyclotron), it's apparent that the furnace door can only withstand the heat flux that is applied without it coming dangerously close to melting.

J.4.2.2 Evaluation process

It is important to use actual load and environmental conditions, such as the coupling device and the test system used for the EUT test, for the evaluation of amplifier linearity. The test arrangement is shown in Figure J.1.

Amplifier linearity shall be evaluated at least at the minimum, middle and maximum frequency range available for the amplifier (linear frequency scale). For example, an amplifier with a frequency range of 0.15 MHz to 80 MHz shall be evaluated at 0,15 MHz, 40 MHz and 80 MHz.

|||||IEC 61000-4-6:2023 © IEC 2023|
| :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: |

NOTE  Evaluation of test data taken on the amplifier can be used to justify the selection of different frequency points.

Signal  Power  Directional Amplifier  Power  Coupler  T2  Coupling  couplerDevelop  Coupling  system  Coupling  device  system  detector  figure  amplifier design process

Amplifier linearity | Amplifier design | Device selection

A linearity test shall be performed in accordance with the following procedure for each frequency as specified above.

1) Determine the signal generator setting necessary to generate both the minimum and maximum levels (see J.4.2.1) for the appropriate coupling device setup.

2) Set the signal generator to the minimum value determined in step 1), and record the output of the signal generator and the forward power of the amplifier.

3) Increase the setting of the signal generator by 1 dB and record the output of the signal generator and the forward power of the amplifier.

4) Repeat steps 2) and 3) until the maximum set value of the signal generator determined in step 1) is reached.

5) Repeat steps 1) to 4) for the remaining frequencies.

J.4.2.3 Linearity criteria

For the results obtained in J.4.2.2, the measured amplifier output shall increase by 1 dB (±1 dB) for each 1 dB increase in the signal generator output (that is, the tolerance of the power amplifier linearity is ±1 dB).

If the measured data obtained following the process specified in J.4.2.2 meets the ±1 dB specification, then the amplifier which the test laboratory uses satisfies the linearity criteria. If the data exceeds this linearity specification, then J.4.2.4 and J.4.2.5 shall also apply.

Figure J.2 shows an example defining the tolerance of +1 dB, -1 dB based on the amplifier output at a single frequency. The signal generator output in this example is varied between a minimum level of -30 dBm and a maximum level of 0 dBm. In this example the amplifier exceeds the tolerance.

J.4.2.5 Immunity test when the amplifier linearity characteristic exceeds the criteria

When the evaluation result of J.4.2.3 does not fulfil the criteria for linearity by ±1 dB, but fulfils the criteria of J.4.2.4, it is necessary to adjust the forward power during actual EUT test by using a system with feedback, in which a power meter is used to monitor the output power from the test generator.

**COMPATIBILITÉ ÉLECTROMAGNÉTIQUE (CEM)**

**Partie 4-6: Techniques d'essai et de mesure**

**Immunité aux perturbations conduites, induites par**

**les champs aux fréquences radioélectriques**


**1 Domaine d'application**

La présente partie de IEIC 61000 traite des exigences relatives à l'immunité en conduction des

matériels électriques et électroniques aux perturbations électromagnétiques provoquées par

des émetteurs radioélectriques (RF) dans la plage de fréquences de 150 kHz à 80 MHz.

NOTE 1 Les comités de produits peuvent également choisir d'utiliser les méthodes décrites dans le présent

document pour les fréquences inférieures ou égales à 230 MHz (voir Annexe B) même si ces méthodes et les

appareils d'essai sont destinés à être utilisés dans la plage de fréquences inférieures ou égales à 80 MHz.

Les matériels qui ne comportent pas au moins un câble conducteur (cordon d'alimentation, ligne

de transmission ou connexion de mise à la terre, par exemple) capable de coupler les matériels

aux champs perturbateurs aux fréquences radioélectriques ne relèvent pas du domaine

d'application du présent document.


NOTE 2 Les méthodes d'essai sont spécifiées dans la présente partie de l'EIC 61000 afin d'évaluer l'incidence des

signaux perturbateurs conduits, induits par les rayonnements électromagnétiques, sur le matériel concerné. La

simulation et le mesurage de ces perturbations conduites ne sont pas parfaitement exacts pour la détermination

quantitative des effets. Les méthodes d'essai spécifiées sont structurées dans l'objectif principal d'établir une

reproductibilité appropriée des résultats dans différentes installations à des fins d'analyse quantitative des effets.

L'objet du présent document est d'établir une référence commune dans le but d'évaluer

l'immunité fonctionnelle des matériels électriques et électroniques, lorsqu'ils sont soumis aux

perturbations conduites induites par les champs aux fréquences radioélectriques. La méthode

d'essai du présent document décrit une méthode cohérente dans le but d'évaluer l'immunité

d'un matériel ou d'un système vis-à-vis d'un phénomène spécifié.


NOTE 3 Comme cela est décrit dans le Guide 107 de l'EIC, le présent document est une publication fondamentale

en CEM destinée à être utilisée par les comités de produits de l'EIC. Comme cela est également indiqué dans le

Guide 107, il incombe aux comités de produits de l'EIC de déterminer s'il convient d'appliquer ou non la présente

norme d'essai d'immunité. Si tel est le cas, ils ont la responsabilité de déterminer les niveaux d'essai et les critères

de performance appropriés.

**2 Références normatives**

Les documents suivants sont cités dans le texte de sorte qu'ils constituent, pour tout ou partie

de leur contenu, des exigences du présent document. Pour les références datées, seule

l'édition citée s'applique. Pour les références non datées, la dernière édition du document de

référence s'applique (y compris les éventuels amendements).

CISPR 16-1-2, _Spécifications des méthodes et des appareils de mesure des perturbations_

_radioélectriques et de l'immunité aux perturbations radioélectriques_  _Partie 1-2:_ _Méthodes de

_mesure des perturbations et de l'immunité_  _Mesures des perturbations conduites_

**4** **Généralités**

La source de perturbations couverte par le présent document est essentiellement un champ
électromagnétique, issu d'émetteurs RF intentionnels, qui peut avoir une incidence sur la
longueur totale des câbles raccordés à des matériels installés. Les dimensions des matériels
perturbés, dans la plupart des cas un sous-ensemble d'un système plus important, sont par
hypothèse réduites par rapport aux longueurs d'onde des signaux brouilleurs. Les conducteurs
entrants et sortants (cordons secteur, lignes de télécommunications, câbles d'interface, par
exemple) se comportent comme des réseaux d'antennes de réception passifs et comme des
chemins conducteurs du signal pour les signaux intentionnels et non intentionnels.

Entre ces réseaux de câbles, les matériels susceptibles sont exposés à des courants qui
circulent "à travers" les matériels. Il est admis par hypothèse que les systèmes de câbles
raccordés à un matériel fonctionnent en mode à résonance (doublets _\A 4,_ _j/2_ ouverts ou repliés);
ils sont donc représentés par des dispositifs de couplage et de découplage dont l'impédance
de mode commun est de 150 Q par rapport à un plan de masse de référence. Pour la méthode
décrite dans le présent document, l'EUT est connecté entre deux liaisons d'impédance de mode
commun de 150 Q, dont l'une fournit une source RF et l'autre un chemin de retour pour le
courant.

Pour cette méthode d'essai, l'EUT est soumis à une source de perturbations comprenant des
champs électriques et magnétiques, qui simulent les perturbations issues d'émetteurs RF
intentionnels. Ces champs perturbateurs _(E_ et _H)_ reproduisent sensiblement les champs
électriques et magnétiques proches qui résultent des tensions et des courants dus au montage
d'essai représenté à la Figure 1.

L'utilisation de dispositifs de couplage et de découplage pour appliquer le signal perturbateur
à un seul câble à la fois, tandis que tous les autres câbles sont maintenus dans un état non
excité (voir Figure 2), ne peut que reproduire sensiblement la situation réelle, où les sources
de perturbations agissent sur l'ensemble des câbles simultanément, avec une plage
d'amplitudes et de phases différentes.

Les dispositifs de couplage et de découplage sont spécifiés en 6.2. Tout dispositif de couplage
et de découplage conforme à ces caractéristiques peut être utilisé. Les réseaux de couplage et
de découplage décrits à l'Annexe C ne sont que des exemples de réseaux disponibles dans le
commerce.

6.2.3.2 Pince de courant

Ce dispositif établit un couplage inductif sur le cbble raccordép a l'EUT.

La pince de courant ne doit pas induire d'affaiblissement significatift. L'augmentation de
I'affaiblissement de transmission du montage d'essai lors de l'insertion d'une pince de courant
ne doit pas depasser 1,6 dB. La Figure 10 represente un circuit pour le montage de verification

de l'affaiblissement de transmission.

NOTE 1 Ces performances peuvent etre verifiees en deux etapes. Au cours de la premiere etape, la pince de
courant n'est pas utilisee et la tension est consignee. Au cours de la seconde etape, la pince de courant est inselee
et son acces d'entree est termine par une impedance de 50 Q, puis la tension est mesuree. La difference entre ces
deux mesures est cornperee a l'exigence de 1,6 dB ci-dessus.

NOTE 2 Par exemple, avec un rapport des nombres de spires de 5:l, I'impedance serie de mode commun
transformee peut etre negligee par rapport a [impedance de 150 Q etablie par l'AE. Dans ce cas, Iimpedance de
sortie du generateur d'essai (50 Q) est transformee en 2 Q. D'autres rapports de nombres de spires peuvent [tire]
utilises.

Le niveau de signal appliqu ep la pince d'injection de courant est regle avant I'essai. La
procédure de reglage du niveau d'essai est specifiee en 6.4.2 et la Figure 10.

NOTE 3 Le cable est generacement positionnee au milieu de la pince pour reduire le plus possible le couplage

### Page 110

value placed on protecting critical infrastructure and ensuring the integrity of supply chains in situations of ongoing conflict, particularly in the West Bank. The scale of the Israeli security assault on Gaza when it was captured by Israeli forces may seem impressively great, but comparing it to the number of device port connectors and termination points present on the Internet's collective infrastructure of devices and port connectors is hard to ignore. Frankly, it feels strangely like our technology is growing weaker and weaker and more vulnerable in the midst of an unfolding war in the neighbourhood of our cities - more so than before.

The signatories of the initial agreement and executive agreement to the second phase of the Connectivity Development Programme in Israel and Palestine by the European Union (EU) associate at its most basic level, for example, is a number representing the number of devices or port connectors involved or that are included in the infrastructure of the Internet in Palestine. The reckoning - what these utterly diverse devices (from Saudi Arabia to South Africa) are actually connected to and their hundreds or thousands of unique device identifiers which are part of what is called the"internet of things," is so diffuse as to render a degree of clarity and detail for the first part of the Programme impossible to ascertain. The EU Draft Agreement contains however an entire chapter on these technological matters, shortly skipping over the internet's indispensable topic altogether. Over the course of the first phase the Union's citizen-funding provider in the region "GIZ", announced a cut to resources to the Authority for the International Development of Protestant-Sectarian Affairs (part of the US Foreign Affairs Community), rather than to the UN.

The Union's communication unit is so overwhelmed and hastily writes another set of chapters on what they're looking at as European text-rules.

It's similarly evident on the pricing side. European energy companies aren't quite certain how they will rank as energy partnerships in a possible truce, based on U.S Secretary of State John Kerry's avowedly blue-green coalition between the UK and Israel, and the UAE. Energy utilities don't feel it's their time to stage pro-EU shows yet until the advancement of U.S crushes as sanctions impoverish the supply chains of the financially-industrial West.

The EU's imagined diplomatic aspect of the Package of Measures is quaint. In reality what it says is, "We're together! pricing up our telecom services, so together, we can connect the world to our companies". What it means, you might think, is that the Union will be promoting to countries that the EU wants to keep, the open, interoperable internet access and infrastructural investments. But the EU isn't allowed to aspire that much, and in fact the EU's language isn't so accommodating when it comes to what it really wants to say, like its rights to prevent internet disconnections and to make desirable access possible.

**7.7** **Application de l'injection directe**

Lorsque l'injection directe est utilisée pour les câbles avec écran, les mesures suivantes doivent
être prises.

-  L'EUT doit être placé sur un support isolant à 0,1 m au-dessus du plan de masse de
référence.

-  Sur le câble soumis à l'essai, une pince de découplage telle que celle spécifiée à
I'Article A.3 doit être placée entre le point d'injection et I'AE, aussi près que possible du
point d'injection. Un deuxième accès de l'EUT doit être chargé à 150 Q (voir 7.5 et Figure 6
pour plus d'informations). Des réseaux de découplage doivent être installés sur tous les
autres câbles connectés à l'EUT. Lorsqu'il est ouvert, un CDN est considéré comme un
réseau de découplage. Voir aussi 6.2.5.

9 issues type fidelity in telecommunication services.As discussed in section II, the transmitter (TX) of the system samples the modulation function (SMDF) with random coefficients and transmits the data while suppressing spurious peaks. The goal is to keep the peaks' amplitudes constant, but to modify their positions, to avoid time-intervals between peaks.

### Figures
Figure 6 attempts to validate Equation (6) in the original article. Although this development is still subject to further investigation, it may play a vital role in providing a realistic image of the system's hypothesis. The majority of the samples in this plot were taken at frequencies between 100 kHz and 100 MHz for the 10 dB VNA, which does not affect the problem detailed in section II.

### Table
Table I shows the simulation results of the system. The simulation is performed for various cases such as 10 dB, 20 dB, 30 dB, etc. The results indicate that the system has good accuracy and fidelity in transmitting video signals. This confirms that the system works as intended, and the novel treatment used in this study creates an image-by-image equalization called clips.

### Conclusion
In conclusion, this study has shown that the novel treatment used in this study keeps the peaks' amplitudes constant while modifying their positions, to avoid time-intervals between peaks, and that the system has good accuracy and fidelity in transmitting video signals.

\[d_z = \max( 25, 100 + 135^{\frac{x-u_{\text{min}}}{\Delta x}} )\]

where the minimum extent \(d_z\) for which Ne.mesh can not compute within a given range of \(x\) is:

Why is \(35^\circ\) fairly close to the real aspect ratio? The reason is the ordering of the variables \(y\) and \(z\) (size coupled to \(\phi\), width coupled to \(\theta\)). Consequently, the projected notation of \(d_z\) will have a value \(z_1\), such that \(d_x = z_1\), \(d_y = y\), and \(d_z = z_1\). Similarly, if \(\theta\) is greater than \(\pi/2\) but smaller than \(\frac{\pi}{2}\), we may consider \(\theta=0\). In this case, the projection of \(d_x\) will have a value less than \(z_1\). However, the latter projection is out of the range \([\theta_{\text{min}},\theta_{\text{max}}]\) that the module uses to project the shape \(z_1\). The inequality also implies that if \(d_z\) is independent of \(\theta\), \(d_x\) and \(d_y\) will still include the same \(25\) as in Fig.2. More details on the projection approach are given in [9].

In the limit case, the projection of \(d_z\) on the \(\phi\) axis is useless. The projection on \(\theta\) is only interesting when \(\theta\leq\pi/2\).

# Annexe C (informatie)

Lignes directrices pour le choix des niveaux d'essai

II convient de choisir les niveaux d'essai en fonction de I'environnement de rayonnements
electronagnetiques auquel peuvent etre exposes l'EUT et les cables dans leur configuration
d'installation definitive. II convient de prendre en compte les consequences des defaillances
lors du choix du niveau d'essai a utiliser. II convient d'envisager un niveau superieur si les
consequences d'une defaillance sont importantes.

Si l'EUT doit etre installe sur un nombre reduit de sites, l'examen des sources radioelectriques
locales permet de calculer 1'intensite des champs susceptibles d'etre rencontres. Si les
puissances des sources ne sont pas connues, il peut etre possible de mesurer 1'intensite reelle
du champ a 1'emplacement ou aux emplacements concernes.

Lorsque les equipements sont destines a fonctionner dans differents sites, les lignes directrices
suivantes peuvent etre suivies pour choisir le niveau d'essai a utiliser.

Les classes suivantes se rapportent aux niveaux enumeres a I'Article 5; elles sont considerees
comme des lignes directrices generales pour le choix des niveaux appropries:

Classe 1: Environnement a rayonnements electronagnetiques faibles. Niveaux types des
stations de radio/television siteues a une distance de plus de 1 km et niveaux
types des emetteurs-recepteurs de faible puissance.

Classe 2: Environnement a rayonnements electronagnetiques moderes. Des emetteurs-
recepteurs portables de faible puissance (generalement inferieure a une
puissance assignee de 1 W) sont utilises, mais avec des restrictions d'emploi a
proximite immediate des materiels. Environnement commercial type.

Classe 3: Environnement a rayonnements electronagnetiques severes. Des emetteurs-
recepteurs portables (2 W et plus) sont utilises a des distances relativement
courtes des materiels, mais pas a moins de 1 m. Des emetteurs de radiodiffusion
de grande puissance se trouvent a proximite immediate des equipements et des
appareils ISM (industriels, scientifiques et medicaux) peuvent etre situes a
proximite. Environnement industriel type.

Classe X: X est un niveau ouvert qui peut etre negocie et specifie dans les specifications
de materiel ou les normes de materiels applicables.

Les niveaux d'essai decrits sont des valeurs types qui sont rarement deposeses dans les
emplacements decrits. A certains emplacements, ces valeurs sont deposesees, par exemple a
proximite des emetteurs de grande puissance ou des appareils ISM situes dans le meme
batiment. Dans de tels cas, il peut etre preferable de blender la piece ou le batiment, et d'installer
des filtres sur les cables de transmission et de puissance connectes aux materiels, plutot que
de specifier I'immunite de tous les materiels vis- a-vis de tels niveaux.

Notte 15 L'incertitude liée au 7.4.1, oü une sonde de contrôle est utilisée et une limitation de courant est appliquée,

n'est pas prise en compte à l'Annexe G. Dans ce cas, la valeur de <div style="font-size: 14px;">U</div> n'est plus la même que celle déterminée lors
de la procédure de réglage du niveau, mais est réduite à une valeur inconnue. Par conséquent, aucune incertitude
ne peut être assignée à <div style="font-size: 14px;">U</div> dans ce cas.

AETERM -- est l'effet de l'impédance de l'AE, qu'il convient de maintenir à 150 Ω (impédance idéale admise par hypothèse de l'EUT). Des écarts par rapport à cette valeur ont une influence significative, principalement dans la plage des fréquences basses (au-dessous de 10 MHz), là où la directivité de la pince EM est faible. Cet écart d'impédance peut avoir un effet significatif sur le niveau d'essai réel. En pratique, la désadaptation d'impédance détermine le pourcentage du signal d'essai qui se dirige vers l'EUT ou vers l'AE. Si l'impédance de l'AE est supérieure à celle de l'EUT, davantage de tension d'essai se dirige vers l'AE plutôt que vers l'EUT. Une valeur plus faible peut être utilisée aux fréquences supérieures à 10 MHz.

Cette contribution peut faire l'objet d'une étude expérimentale à l'aide d'un analyseur de réseau. Le facteur de couplage de la pince peut être mesuré pour une impédance de l'AE de 150 Ω et comparé à différentes impédances de l'AE.

3) Bilan d'incertitude lorsqu'une pince de courant est utilisée

Le Tableau G.5 et le Tableau G.6 donnent des exemples de bilans d'incertitude pour le réglage du niveau de tension et pour l'essai avec une pince de courant.

Fonction modèle pour le processus de réglage du niveau de la tension avec une pince de courant (toutes les grandeurs sont exprimées en unités logarithmiques):

\]

\]

NOTE 18 Les contributions de LMC ou du générateur d’essai (TG) sont indiquées dans le Tableau G.5 et le
Tableau G.6 pour le réglage du niveau ou pour l’essai, ou pour les deux, en fonction de l’utilisation ou non d’une
boucle de commande pour le générateur de signaux et le niveau de sortie de l’amplificateur. Dans cet exemple, le
générateur d’essai ne contribue pas au bilan d’incertitude, car il fait partie de la boucle de commande. La contribution
de la boucle de commande est établie par l’appareil de mesure (voir aussi la Note 19). Cependant, le générateur
d’essai est inclus dans le Tableau G.5 et le Tableau G.6 afin de rappeler aux laboratoires d’essai qu’ils peuvent tenir
compte de ce paramètre, en fonction du montage d’essai particulier du laboratoire. L’explication des termes fournit
une explication et des recommandations concernant l’analyse de la contribution du TG.

NOTE 19 Si le même matériel est utilisé pour le réglage du niveau et pour les essais, seules les contributions de
répétabilité et de linéarité sont indiquées dans le Tableau G.6 pour le processus d’essai. La contribution pour le
réglage du niveau peut être négligée.

NOTE 20 Cette contribution est normalement nulle dans le Tableau G.5, dans la mesure où elle est intégrée au
résultat du processus de réglage du niveau du fait de la boucle de commande. Si un circuit différent est utilisé pour
le réglage du niveau et pour l’essai, l’influence des différents montages et la reproductibilité du montage d’essai
contribuent à cette source d’incertitude dans le Tableau G.6. Si le même circuit est utilisé pour le réglage du niveau
et pour les essais, alors ces contributions peuvent être ignorées.

L'incertitude de mesure est calculée en unités logarithmiques pour assurer son homogénéité avec les contributions d'incertitude à l'incertitude de niveau d'essai (spécification de l'amplitude du voltmètre et étalonnage de l'affaiblissement d'insertion de l'adaptateur, par exemple); elle est généralement exprimée en dB. La meilleure estimation doit donc être aussi exprimée en unités logarithmiques (dB(μV), par exemple).

Le niveau de tension d'essai doit être consigné en fonction de la meilleure estimation de la tension et de son incertitude élargie. La meilleure estimation doit être la moyenne de la tension \(U_0\) sur la plage de fréquences considérée.

<|ref|>text<|/ref|><|det|>[[139, 224, 910, 278]]<|/det|>
L'experience montre que certains EUT spécifiques peuvent réagir de façon plus sensible aux signaux RF, lorsque l'injection est réalisée sur un seul accès et qu'un autre accès identique est chargé. Les comités de produits peuvent décider d'utiliser la méthode décrite à l'Annexe I au lieu de la procédure décrite dans la partie principale du présent document.

<|ref|>text<|/ref|><|det|>[[139, 300, 909, 352]]<|/det|>
L'Annexe I donne des informations sur les essais des accès lorsqu'un EUT comporte plusieurs accès identiques. L'Annexe I décrit une méthode d'injection, où le signal RF est injecté dans l'un de ces accès identiques et où l'impédance de terminaison est placée sur un autre de ces accès au lieu d'être placée sur l'accès choisi conformément au 7.5.

<|ref|>text<|/ref|><|det|>[[139, 373, 909, 413]]<|/det|>
Les essais sont réalisés en complément que les accés spécifiés en 7.5 afin d'évaluer l'immunité de l'EUT aux signaux RF induits sur un accès et acheminés vers un autre accès identique.

<|ref|>text<|/ref|><|det|>[[139, 434, 909, 474]]<|/det|>
Le réseau local (Ethernet, etc.), les entrées de température Pt100, les entrées/sorties analogiques, les entrées/sorties numériques et les entrées de compteur de tachymètre peuvent constituer des exemples d'accès identiques.

<|ref|>title<|/ref|><|det|>[[139, 496, 743, 509]]<|/det|>
## I.2 Montage d'essai pour l'injection sur des accès identiques

<|ref|>sub_title<|/ref|><|det|>[[139, 527, 364, 540]]<|/det|>
## I.2.1 Choix des accès

<|ref|>text<|/ref|><|det|>[[139, 554, 910, 607]]<|/det|>
L'injection est réalisée entre deux types d'accès identiques. Les deux accès choisis pour les essais sont deux accès placés le plus près possible l'un de l'autre. Plusieurs groupes d'ensembles identiques d'accès peuvent exister sur l'EUT; dans ce cas, des ensembles de chaque type d'accès sont choisis pour les essais.

<|ref|>text<|/ref|><|det|>[[139, 627, 909, 667]]<|/det|>
NOTE Un comité de produit peut spécifier que les essais ne sont exigés que pour les types spécifiques d'interfaces ou de câbles, ou que les essais ne sont exigés que pour les accès avec des câbles dépassant une certaine longueur. L'Annexe I ne s'applique qu'aux accès choisis pour les essais. Le comité de produit est invité à tenir compte également de tous les modes des cartes d'E/S polyvalentes.

<|ref|>sub_title<|/ref|><|det|>[[139, 679, 546, 691]]<|/det|>
## I.2.2 Procédure d'injection d'accès à accès

<|ref|>text<|/ref|><|det|>[[139, 707, 909, 732]]<|/det|>
Un accès est choisi comme accès d'injection. L'autre accès est choisi comme accès de terminaison, sur lequel est connectée la terminaison de 50 Ω sur le CDN. Voir Figure I.1.

<|ref|>text<|/ref|><|det|>[[139, 752, 909, 792]]<|/det|>
Conformément au corps principal du présent document, tous les autres accès EUT sont équipés de CDN utilisés comme dispositifs de découplage, la terminaison de 50 Ω n'étant pas connectée, comme cela est spécifié dans le corps principal du présent document.

<|ref|>text<|/ref|><|det|>[[139, 813, 909, 839]]<|/det|>
Si plusieurs types d'accès sont disponibles pour l'objet à l'essai, les essais sont également répétés sur un ensemble de ces autres types d'accès.

<|ref|>text<|/ref|><|det|>[[139, 860, 909, 897]]<|/det|>
Si les essais sur les accès identiques ne peuvent être réalisés à l'aide des CDN, les règles générales de l'Article 7 s'appliquent à l'injection sur les accès identiques. La Figure 20 donne des recommandations pour le choix de la méthode d'injection.

<|ref|>text<|/ref|><|det|>[[139, 918, 909, 943]]<|/det|>
Les essais sur les accès et le traitement des résultats d'essai sont réalisés comme cela est décrit dans le corps principal du présent document.

Johlander先生，将在公元1634年测量柑橘的甜度，获得了以下结果：当柑橘的浓度增加到6倍时，甜度加倍，甜度增加到18倍。换句话说，柑橘上的甜度增加了一倍。然而，这些发现被永久放弃了，因为当时的科学家认为柑橘的自然 sweetness 与柑橘中的糖浓度无关。
